nightly-azure-canary.note: RETIRED 2026-08-28, UNTRACKED (the "kind":"nightly-workflow" tag is deliberately removed): .github/workflows/nightly-azure-canary.yml was DELETED outright (Azure permanently gone since 2026-08-13; see skills/azure-canary/SKILL.md's SUPERSEDED banner and its AWS-era successors aws-dr-canary/aws-image-canary/nightly-schedule-canary). A deleted workflow can never beat again, so leaving this tagged "kind":"nightly-workflow" would make schedule-canary.mjs correctly-but-uselessly flag it DEAD forever and page every nightly sentinel run -- the exact anti-pattern the "azure-watchdog" comment on a sibling entry below already describes avoiding for a never-scheduled workflow. KEPT (untracked) only as the anchor several sibling entries below still point to ("see nightly-azure-canary's entry above") for the shared design rationale, preserved here verbatim: ITEM 2.3 (Wave 2, AI-OS research-pass 2026-07-21) schedule-liveness heartbeats answer 'did the workflow's cron fire at all', a DIFFERENT failure class than 'did its content check go red' (GitHub disables a schedule after 60 days of repo inactivity; the workflow YAML could be deleted or malformed; a cron typo could make it never match, and none of that ever shows up as a red run, because a workflow that never runs never gets a chance to go red). 1560min = 26h SLO convention: a daily job gets one occasional-delay cycle of slack before it counts as LATE (heartbeat.mjs's own status math: LATE once age exceeds interval_min, DEAD past 3x).
